We further show that this structure persists upon breaking integrability with a transverse field, with the periodic orbits continuing to govern the dynamics. Our results establish a direct connection between the periodic-orbit picture of quantum scarring and the algebraic structure of integrable models, showing that key features of scar dynamics can be understood analytically within the Bethe ansatz framework.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a periodic-orbit framework in the integrable XYZ/XXZ spin-1/2 chain to identify quantum many-body scars, reconstructs scarred eigenstates via Bethe ansatz with zero-momentum magnon pairs, explains equidistant tower spacing analytically, and shows persistence under integrability-breaking perturbations.
AI.motivation: To understand the relationship between quantum many-body scars and integrability, and to develop an analytical framework that connects periodic-orbit scarring with the Bethe ansatz structure.
AI.method: Periodic-orbit framework applied to integrable XYZ/XXZ spin-1/2 chain; Bethe-ansatz quantum number analysis; analytical decoupling of zero-momentum magnon pairs in Bethe equations; integrability-breaking perturbation with a transverse field.
AI.result: Identified families of scarred periodic orbits; reconstructed scarred eigenstates and towers within Bethe ansatz; explained equidistant tower spacing from decoupling of zero-momentum magnon pairs; showed scar structure persists under transverse field perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Direct connection established between periodic-orbit quantum scarring and integrable model algebra; key scar dynamics features are analytically tractable within Bethe ansatz.

title: Superadditivity for Entanglement-Assisted Communication
summary: The entanglement-assisted capacity of a quantum channel admits an additive single-letter characterization, implying that joint encodings across channel uses cannot increase the ultimate communication rate. Here, we show that this additive picture does not extend to communication reliability. Specifically, we prove that the Petz-Rényi channel information can be strictly superadditive for every $α\in[1/2,1)$, yielding a genuine multi-copy enhancement of the entanglement-assisted random-coding error exponent, even though the entanglement-assisted capacity remains additive. We establish this phenomenon analytically already for measurement channels, which are entanglement-breaking and have additive unassisted capacity. Remarkably, this strict superadditivity is witnessed by a separable, classically correlated two-copy channel-input marginal, demonstrating that no entanglement between the transmitted systems is required. Our results show that, although correlations across channel uses cannot increase the ultimate rate of entanglement-assisted communication, they can enhance its reliability.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that while entanglement-assisted capacity is additive (no multi-copy rate enhancement), the random-coding error exponent can be strictly superadditive for α∈[1/2,1), meaning joint encodings across channel uses can enhance communication reliability even without entanglement between copies. This is shown analytically for measurement channels.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the additive single-letter characterization of entanglement-assisted capacity extends to communication reliability, specifically whether multi-copy joint encodings can improve the error exponent.
AI.method: Analytical proof using Petz-Rényi channel information for α∈[1/2,1), demonstrated on measurement channels (entanglement-breaking with additive unassisted capacity) using separable, classically correlated two-copy channel-input marginals.
AI.result: Strict superadditivity of the Petz-Rényi channel information is proven for α∈[1/2,1), meaning joint encodings genuinely enhance the entanglement-assisted random-coding error exponent despite additive capacity.
AI.conclusion: Correlations across channel uses cannot increase the ultimate rate of entanglement-assisted communication but can enhance its reliability, and this phenomenon requires no entanglement between transmitted systems.

title: LDGM-Based Quantum Codes for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
summary: We construct a new family of Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes using the generator and parity-check matrices of Low-Density Generator Matrix (LDGM) codes, with row operations applied to both matrices in order to achieve the desired quantum rate. Decoding is performed in an iterative manner, by applying message passing over the associated graph, and discrete Density Evolution (DDE) is used to optimize performance in the depolarizing channel. The proposed construction offers high flexibility and easiness in the design, producing quantum codes that possess excellent error correction capabilities. By properly designing the structure of the code, we are able to control and bound the weight of the stabilizer generators to a small value, which results in codes particularly well suited for fault-tolerant quantum computation. At the same time, these codes achieve very good performance in terms of error correction capability.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a new family of CSS codes built from LDGM codes, using message-passing decoding and discrete Density Evolution optimization for the depolarizing channel, achieving excellent error correction with low-weight stabilizer generators suitable for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
AI.motivation: To construct CSS codes that are highly flexible, easy to design, and possess excellent error correction capabilities while keeping stabilizer generator weights low for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
AI.method: The construction uses generator and parity-check matrices of LDGM codes with row operations to achieve desired quantum rates; decoding employs iterative message passing over the associated graph, and performance is optimized via discrete Density Evolution (DDE) for the depolarizing channel.
AI.result: The proposed codes achieve excellent error correction performance, with low-weight stabilizer generators that are well suited for fault-tolerant quantum computation, alongside high design flexibility.
AI.conclusion: The new CSS-LDGM code family offers a practical, flexible design with strong error correction and low-weight stabilizers, making it promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing applications.

title: Parameter-Shift Rules for Gradients in Boson Sampling Experiments
summary: Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive $n-$th order parameter-shift rules for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where $n$ photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that in general it is not possible to generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling. Only in the specific case where the transmission matrix of the interferometer can be factorized as a diagonal loss matrix premultiplied by a pure unitary it is possible to obtain parameter-shift rules with a finite order given by twice the total number of photons detected. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method by comparing its performance against finite differences on real hardware.

AI.tldr: The paper derives parameter-shift rules for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities under photon loss, shows limitations for Gaussian boson sampling, and demonstrates efficacy on real hardware.
AI.motivation: To enable gradient-based optimization in photonic quantum experiments, the authors aim to derive parameter-shift rules in the presence of photon loss, which is a realistic and unavoidable experimental imperfection.
AI.method: The authors use a robust photon loss model to derive $n-$th order parameter-shift rules for Fock boson sampling transition probabilities. They analyze the general impossibility of extending this to Gaussian boson sampling, and identify a special factorizable case where finite-order rules exist.
AI.result: Parameter-shift rules of order $n$ are obtained for Fock boson sampling with $n$ photons in a lossy interferometer. For Gaussian boson sampling, such rules are not generally possible; only when the transmission matrix factorizes as a diagonal loss matrix times a unitary can rules of order twice the photon count be derived. The method outperforms finite differences on real hardware.
AI.conclusion: Parameter-shift differentiation is feasible for lossy Fock boson sampling but has fundamental limitations for Gaussian boson sampling, with a special structured case allowing a finite-order gradient recipe.

title: Backpropagating Pauli Propagation
summary: We develop a backpropagation algorithm for evaluating parameter gradients in quantum circuits using Pauli propagation simulation. The method has computational complexity comparable to that of standard sparse Pauli simulation techniques, while producing gradients whose accuracy is of the same order as the corresponding observable expectation values. By exploiting the reversibility of quantum circuits, the algorithm reduces the memory cost by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(n_\text{param})$ compared with conventional reverse-mode automatic differentiation, where $n_\text{param}$ denotes the number of parameters in the circuit. Compared with finite difference methods, the algorithm is $\mathcal{O}(n_\text{param})$ more efficient in function evaluations. These features enable efficient and accurate classical optimization of quantum circuits for applications such as state preparation and time-evolution compression, while also allowing operator-complexity measures such as the operator stabilizer Rényi entropy to be monitored and regularized during optimization. We demonstrate the method by optimizing low-energy state-preparation circuits for transverse-field Ising models in one, two, and three dimensions and for the three-dimensional Heisenberg model, and by compressing two-dimensional time-evolution circuits.

AI.tldr: A backpropagation algorithm for quantum circuit gradients using Pauli propagation simulation with improved memory and computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: To enable efficient and accurate classical optimization of quantum circuits by reducing memory cost and computational complexity compared to existing methods like reverse-mode automatic differentiation and finite difference methods.
AI.method: Develops a backpropagation algorithm leveraging Pauli propagation simulation and reversibility of quantum circuits to compute parameter gradients with complexity comparable to sparse Pauli simulation, reducing memory cost by O(n_param) and function evaluations by O(n_param).
AI.result: Demonstrated the method by optimizing low-energy state-preparation circuits for transverse-field Ising models in 1D, 2D, and 3D, and for the 3D Heisenberg model, and by compressing 2D time-evolution circuits.
AI.conclusion: The algorithm enables efficient classical optimization of quantum circuits for state preparation and time-evolution compression, while allowing operator-complexity measures like operator stabilizer Rényi entropy to be monitored and regularized during optimization.

title: Entanglement Detection for Two-Qubit and Three-Qubit Pure States via Unitary Transformations and Ancilla State Measurements
summary: Quantum entanglement is the fundamental hallmark of quantum mechanics and a core resource for realizing long-distance quantum communication and scalable linear quantum computing. Accordingly, the precise detection and quantitative quantification of entanglement constitute a foundational and critical problem in quantum information theory. To date, researchers have proposed numerous sufficient conditions for entanglement detection as well as a variety of entanglement measures to characterize the entanglement strength of quantum states; nevertheless, efficient and direct measurement schemes for core entanglement parameters remain underdeveloped. Based on unitary transformations and auxiliary measurements, this paper proposes a set of quantum circuit schemes capable of directly measuring the bipartite concurrence and the tripartite 3-tangle entanglement measure. By introducing auxiliary qubits and constructing specific controlled unitary operations, the proposed scheme maps the analytical expressions of the two entanglement measures onto the measurement probabilities of output states from quantum circuits. It enables efficient and direct quantitative measurement of bipartite and tripartite entanglement without performing full quantum state tomography. This work provides a feasible technical route for the experimental characterization of entanglement properties and lays a groundwork for the practical deployment of multipartite entanglement resources in quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes quantum circuit schemes using unitary transformations and auxiliary measurements to directly measure bipartite concurrence and tripartite 3-tangle entanglement, eliminating the need for full quantum state tomography.
AI.motivation: Entanglement detection and quantification are fundamental to quantum information theory, but existing methods lack efficient and direct measurement schemes for core entanglement parameters.
AI.method: The schemes introduce auxiliary qubits and construct specific controlled unitary operations to map the analytical expressions of concurrence and 3-tangle onto measurement probabilities of output states from quantum circuits.
AI.result: The proposed approach enables efficient, direct quantitative measurement of bipartite and tripartite entanglement without performing full quantum state tomography.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a feasible technical route for experimental entanglement characterization and lays groundwork for deploying multipartite entanglement resources in quantum information processing.

title: Counterexamples to additivity of minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy of quantum channels for $p>3/4$ and $0\leq p<1/4$
summary: Additivity of minimum output entropies is a central problem in quantum information theory. Nonadditivity is known for every Rényi order $p>1$, at the von Neumann point $p=1$, and near $p=0$, while most of the interval $0<p<1$ has remained open. We prove that for every Rényi order $p$ satisfying either $p>3/4$ or $0\leq p<1/4$, there exist finite-dimensional projection-induced quantum channels such that additivity of the minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy fails. The proof combines two correlated random-projection constructions: a product-conjugate Bell-state witness for $p>3/4$, and a transpose-complement rank-defect witness for $p<1/4$. Thus the unresolved part of $0<p<1$ is reduced to $[1/4,3/4]$. Our estimates also improve the output dimension threshold for additivity violation of minimum output von Neumann entropy, first established in Belinschi, Collins and Nechida.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that additivity of minimum output Rényi entropy fails for all p > 3/4 and 0 ≤ p < 1/4 via two random-projection constructions, narrowing the open interval for p ∈ (0,1) to [1/4, 3/4].
AI.motivation: Additivity of minimum output entropies is a central open problem in quantum information theory, with nonadditivity known for p > 1, p = 1, and near p = 0, but most of the interval 0 < p < 1 remained unresolved.
AI.method: The proof combines two correlated random-projection constructions: a product-conjugate Bell-state witness for p > 3/4, and a transpose-complement rank-defect witness for p < 1/4, both applied to finite-dimensional projection-induced quantum channels.
AI.result: For every Rényi order p satisfying p > 3/4 or 0 ≤ p < 1/4, there exist finite-dimensional projection-induced quantum channels violating additivity of the minimum output p-Rényi entropy. The unresolved interval is reduced to [1/4, 3/4]. The estimates also improve the output dimension threshold for additivity violation of minimum output von Neumann entropy.
AI.conclusion: The work significantly narrows the open region for additivity violation in the Rényi entropy hierarchy, demonstrating nonadditivity over most of the parameter range and improving prior bounds on the von Neumann entropy case.

title: Coulomb blockade in microscopic material defects as a source of decoherence and noise in solid-state quantum circuits
summary: A critical limitation of solid-state quantum devices arises from the materials from which they are fabricated: uncontrolled surfaces, interfaces, and structural imperfections introduce numerous sources of loss and decoherence. Despite extensive efforts, linking these decoherence mechanisms to their microscopic material origins -- essential for developing effective mitigation strategies -- remains an outstanding challenge that has slowed coherence improvements. Here, using scanning gate microscopy on live superconducting circuits we identify a previously unrecognised decoherence mechanism originating from Coulomb blockade and microwave-driven charge tunnelling in metallic grains. Such grains are ubiquitous in thin-film devices fabricated by standard lithography processes. By characterising multiple defects across different devices, we find such defects to be as common and as debilitating to device performance as two-level system (TLS) defects, while originating from a fundamentally different physical mechanism. Importantly, conventional characterisation techniques would misattribute this loss to other, microwave power-independent processes. Our observations thus reveal a widespread source of decoherence in superconducting circuits, challenging the prevailing paradigm that coherence lifetimes are primarily limited by TLS defects. Eliminating metallic grains during fabrication provides a clear and practical route to suppress this mechanism, offering a pathway towards improved coherence and reduced noise in microwave-based solid-state quantum devices.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies metallic grains in superconducting circuits as a previously unrecognized decoherence mechanism via Coulomb blockade and charge tunnelling, challenging the prevailing belief that two-level system defects are the primary coherence limiters.
AI.motivation: Linking decoherence mechanisms in solid-state quantum devices to their microscopic material origins remains a major challenge that has slowed coherence improvements.
AI.method: Scanning gate microscopy on live superconducting circuits was used to identify and characterize decoherence from Coulomb blockade and microwave-driven charge tunnelling in metallic grains.
AI.result: Metallic grains are as common and debilitating as TLS defects but originate from a fundamentally different physical mechanism; conventional techniques would misattribute this loss to other processes.
AI.conclusion: Eliminating metallic grains during fabrication provides a practical route to suppress this decoherence mechanism, improving coherence and reducing noise in microwave-based quantum devices.

title: Dynamic Entanglement Distribution for Multi-User and Multi-Protocol Quantum Networking
summary: Dynamic entanglement distribution is a key requirement for scalable, multi-user and multi-protocol quantum networks. We demonstrate a metropolitan-scale entanglement-based quantum communication network enabled by a quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM), which dynamically distributes polarisation-entangled photon pairs from a broadband source to six users over deployed campus and metropolitan fibre. The network supports programmable full-mesh, partial-mesh and sliced sub-network configurations, enabling flexible allocation of entanglement resources according to link condition and service requirement. We demonstrate stable six-user full-mesh operation over more than 150 hours, compare full-mesh and time-shared partial-mesh strategies under different source and detector conditions, and realise quantum network slicing with optional/additional interconnection links. We also show that the same infrastructure can support different quantum protocols by showcasing Secure Inaugural Authentication-Transfer (SIAT) combined with Network flooding over multiple paths to improve the security of onboarding a new user. These results demonstrate a q-ROADM-enabled entanglement distribution architecture as a novel route towards reconfigurable, service-oriented quantum networking over optical fibre infrastructure.

AI.tldr: A metropolitan-scale entanglement-based quantum network using a quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM) dynamically distributes polarization-entangled photon pairs to six users over deployed fiber, supporting full-mesh, partial-mesh, and sliced sub-network configurations with stable operation over 150+ hours and multi-protocol capability.
AI.motivation: Scalable, multi-user quantum networks require dynamic entanglement distribution, which existing static architectures cannot efficiently support for reconfigurable, service-oriented quantum networking over deployed optical fiber infrastructure.
AI.method: A quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM) dynamically routes polarization-entangled photon pairs from a broadband source to six users over campus and metropolitan fiber, enabling programmable full-mesh, partial-mesh, and sliced sub-network topologies.
AI.result: Stable six-user full-mesh operation over 150+ hours; comparison of full-mesh vs. time-shared partial-mesh strategies under varied source/detector conditions; demonstration of quantum network slicing with interconnection links; and multi-protocol support via SIAT combined with Network flooding for secure user onboarding.
AI.conclusion: The q-ROADM-enabled architecture provides a novel, reconfigurable route towards scalable, service-oriented quantum networking over existing optical fiber infrastructure.
